title: Crush-resistant air sacs allow insect larvae to exploit aquatic habitats at extreme depth.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed all 9 small files from the Dryad deposit (CC0 licence) and read every row count and column: Data_S1 lakefly acoustic layers 62 rows x 25 cols; Data_S2 fish tracks 213,945 rows x 16 cols (19 rows carry a -9999 sentinel for missing values); Data_S3 water-quality sonde profile 261 rows; Data_S4 crush depth 206 rows x 4 cols from 161 unique larvae across 5 Chaoborus species and instars 2-4 plus pupae, depth of failure 7.3-570.8 m; Data_S5 air-sac area vs pressure 909 rows but only 58 distinct air sacs from 32 larvae; Data_S6 81 rows; Data_S7 274 rows; Data_S8 10 rows. Also read the 15.7 kB README, which documents every column and its units.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Science full text is paywalled and not in PubMed Central, so the abstract plus the Dryad README were the only narrative sources. I did not open AZFP_Data.zip (12.91 GB of proprietary .01A raw echosounder binaries); its size and format come from the Dryad file listing and README.

a1_downloadable.note: Dryad deposit doi:10.5061/dryad.4tmpg4fqk, CC0, no login. The site sits behind a bot challenge, but all 9 small files downloaded intact with sizes matching the Dryad file listing.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: For the air-sac project the label is a real column: depth.m (crush depth) in Data_S4 and Area (air-sac profile area) in Data_S5-S8. For the only large table, Data_S2 fish tracks, there is no outcome column at all - any label (species, prey encounter) would have to be constructed by joining tracks to lakefly layers on time and depth.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs are plain columns I read in the files: species name, instar stage, applied pressure in psi, pH, air-sac length and width in mm. No identifier lookups needed.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated in both the README and column names and are consistent: metres, mm, mm^2, psi, pH units, dB re 1 m^2 for target strength. I confirmed value ranges are consistent with those units.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL, verified by counting. Every table with a measured label is far under the ~1,500-row bar: crush depth 206 rows from 161 larvae; air-sac compression 909 rows but only 58 independent sacs (the rest are repeated pressure steps on the same sac); pH series 81, 274 and 10 rows; acoustic layers 62 rows with a 3-class visually assigned label. The one large table (213,945 fish tracks) has no label.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~35 MB of CSV for all usable tables; 12.91 GB zip of raw sonar ignored
a6_fits_laptop.note: The small tables fit in memory trivially. The raw acoustic archive is 12.91 GB of proprietary binary, over the 50 MB download rule and the laptop working-set guidance.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: File sizes match the Dryad API listing exactly and the README's per-file column descriptions match the parsed headers. The paywalled article text could not be cross-checked for sample sizes.

a8_label_provenance.note: Crush depth and air-sac area are direct physical measurements (pressure chamber to implosion; imaged sac profile), not model outputs. The exception is Data_S1's DVM stage, which the README says was assigned 'based on visual examination' and is largely derivable from the depth and acceleration columns beside it.

existing_models.name: Brautaset et al. deep convolutional network for acoustic target classification (ICES Journal of Marine Science, 2020)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved beyond the search result title and abstract snippet; I did not open the paper, so I quote no number.

backbone.name: None applicable
backbone.hardware: CPU only; no sequence, molecule or image data for any open backbone to encode

integration.partner_dataset: None identified: the data carries no standard biological identifier (no UniProt, Ensembl, InChIKey or NCBI taxonomy ID), only free-text species abbreviations like 'C. edulis'.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written - no joinable key exists, so any partner resource would need a species-name mapping built by hand for 5 midge species.

controls.positive_control: Crush depth should rise monotonically with instar, which the paper already reports - so a model that recovers it adds nothing.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling across the 161 larvae is runnable but meaningless at this sample size.
controls.external_validation: None found: no second dataset measures Chaoborus air-sac implosion pressure.

honest_claim_h3: A model here could only claim 'the implosion depth of a Chaoborus air sac can be read off its species and instar for the 5 species and 161 larvae measured in one study' - which is a lookup table, not a model.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use midge larva species, developmental stage and air-sac size to predict the water depth at which its air sac implodes.
plain_idea.train_on: Species name, instar (developmental stage 2-4 or pupa) and, where available, air-sac length and width in millimetres. I verified only 206 crush-depth measurements from 161 individual larvae exist.
plain_idea.predict: The simulated freshwater depth in metres at which the air sac or respiratory horn failed, measured directly by raising hydrostatic pressure in a chamber until the sac imploded (7.3-570.8 m across the dataset).
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Insect physiologists and freshwater ecologists would like a rule for how deep a given lake-fly larva can go, but with two usable features and 206 rows the honest answer is a two-column table of group means, not a learned model.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: (1) regress air-sac implosion depth on species and instar - 206 rows, 2 features, a group-mean lookup table does the whole job; (2) classify the diel-migration stage of an acoustic lake-fly layer - 62 rows with a visually assigned label that is nearly computable from the depth and acceleration columns next to it; (3) use the 213,945 fish tracks - no label column exists, so the target would have to be constructed by matching tracks to prey layers on time and depth, which is exactly the Part A2 failure mode.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from actually loading every file: the biggest usable table is a 34 MB CSV that pandas read in a couple of seconds; nothing here needs more than a laptop minute. No timing of a model was done because no model is warranted.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count rows and independent individuals in Data_S4 and Data_S5 - done, and it killed the project: 206 crush-depth rows from 161 larvae, and 909 compression rows from only 58 distinct air sacs.

verdict_reason: Fails A5 on verified counts: the only measured labels sit in 10-206 row tables (161 larvae), and the single large table, 213,945 fish tracks, has no outcome column, so a target would have to be constructed. Beautifully documented CC0 data and a lovely piece of biology, but it is a physiology experiment with 5 species and 2 usable features - a group-mean lookup table, not a machine-learning project. No open-weight backbone fits the data type and no standard identifier exists for integration.
